Major Questions?
❖Looking into varieties of objects present in real world, the following questions 
arises:
▪ How can we represent these objects with their characteristics such that the 
rendered objects look more realistic?
▪ How can we model them that can make the process of rendering efficient?
❖ In order to solve the above problems, there are several methods that are 
broadly categorized into four classes:
▪ Point-sample rendering 
▪ Boundary representation
▪ Space partitioning 
▪ Sweep representation

❖ Point-sample rendering : 
▪ Capture raw data : color, surface normal vector, and 
depth information with the help of input sensing 
devices (range sensor).
▪ Computer vision techniques can be used to find depth 
information of a scene object.
▪ The above information is captured in the form of 
points on the scene, with each point having the 
information as attributes. 
• Color, depth, texture, surface normal, etc.
▪ Such points are further processed to generate 
(synthesize) the scene.

Polygonal-type surfaces (meshes)

Polygonal-type surfaces (Meshes) 
❖ Triangular meshes are generally used to represent object surfaces. Why?
❖ However, other meshes such as quadrilaterals (rectangle, square, rhombs, 
trapezium, and etc.), convex polygon (n-gons) can also be used to 
represent object surfaces.
❖ The reason for using simple polygon in object representation is that it 
simplifies rendering process (the process of synthesizing a photorealistic 
image from a 2D or 3D models).
❖ As we know, rendering is a complex process and requires so much of 
computing resources in terms of hardware and software.
❖ Hence, it is being suggested not to use complex polygons (irregular 
polygons) to represent object surfaces.

Summary of Mesh Representation
❖ The mesh representation is the most basic form of object representation.
❖ All the object representation techniques necessarily converted to mesh 
representation at the end of pipeline before the objects to be rendered.
❖ Common issues with mesh representations:
❖ No. of polygon surfaces : the answer is obvious i.e., more is the no. of 
meshes better is the representation.
❖ Need more memory space to store information related to all meshes. 
❖ Complexity and processing time also depends on no. of meshes. 
❖So, the subdivision rule is important to optimize space and time 
complexities of mesh representation and usually depends on the 
application and resources available.

❖However, for realistic, we want to mimic actual objects rather than its
